notes.text: Prepared detailed implementation plan at 2eb1f06640c6254f14e4b9b7ce7f20b0836bb2bb after compact MCP and runtime operations merged. NOTE-20260908-portable-verification-plan specifies separate producer/consumer CI jobs, copied standalone smoke harness, tarball checksums, native dependency installation, installed CLI/default assets/MCP flow and owned cleanup. Source inspection confirms absent tracked workflow, package allowlist, explicit data/state paths, foreground service-mode access record and offline/live CLI gateway. No package install, build, smoke run, CI workflow or deployment was performed in this planning task. Item remains open, priority next.

problem: The checkout has pnpm check and build scripts but no checked-in GitHub Actions workflow. Repeating broad manual validation costs time, and a passing source checkout does not prove a new user can run the packed CLI and dashboard.

risk.rollback: Revert the focused implementation change without changing existing project configuration or unrelated runtime ownership.

scope: Add one small CI workflow using the supported pnpm check and build commands, a pinned package-manager setup, and cancellation of superseded runs.

Pack the built artifact and install it into an isolated prefix outside the source tree. Smoke-test CLI discovery, static dashboard assets, and an isolated controller with fixture repositories and temporary ports/state.

Exercise the documented install -> register repository -> inspect/claim through MCP path without printing credentials. Preserve shell-free commands and no automatic dependency installation inside managed projects.

Keep CI independent of the owner's filesystem, local Hub checkout, running service, systemd policies, credentials, and private repositories. Any backlog validation step must use a pinned, portable validator setup.

Use Linux for the first repeatable smoke path. Add macOS coverage only for supported behavior that needs it; service-manager integration validation remains in its existing item. Do not publish npm packages or change installed services as a CI side effect.

Read notes/NOTE-20260908-portable-verification-plan/implementation-plan.md before implementation. It defines the proposed two-job workflow, standalone finite smoke command, consumer installation, fixture flow and failure criteria at baseline 2eb1f06.

Produce one checksummed tarball after sequential check/build, then test it in a fresh dependent CI job with no repository checkout. Transfer only the tarball, standalone smoke harness and provenance manifest; never reuse source node_modules or build assets in the consumer.

Exercise a real production dependency installation including native better-sqlite3, exact installed CLI resolution, offline registration and live-controller CLI forwarding, packaged default web-root asset delivery, and actual MCP claim/start/restart/stop/release behavior on a dependency-free fixture.

Use explicit temporary data/state paths, foreground service-mode/no-open output behavior, loopback fixture ports and tracked child ownership. No service-manager installation, user HOME/config changes, managed personal projects or automatic installs inside the generated fixture.

Add meaningful harness fault injection, finite stage budgets and cleanup assertions. Upload only bounded sanitized evidence, preserving a failed outcome for forced cleanup, missing assets, dependency failures or survivor processes.

Keep application behavior checks distinct from static asset delivery and full browser QA. Leave npm publication, platform/service-manager expansion and portable Hub validator acquisition outside this initial workflow.
source: Repository assessment and owner direction on 2026-09-05
title: Automate portable checks and a clean package smoke test
validation: Run checks/build/package installation in an isolated environment without access to the checkout's dependencies or state, and verify the executable serves packaged assets.
Verify missing assets, a failed check, a spawned fixture left alive, or failed cleanup makes the job fail; never label a restarted process as a completed check.
Inspect the package and CI output for accidental state, credentials, logs, or host paths. Document one finite smoke command usable locally and in CI.

Prove the CI consumer job has no checkout and installs the exact upstream artifact checksum with production dependencies. Verify native SQLite loads without source dependency fallback; record runtime/package-manager and installed dependency evidence.

Validate the archive allowlist and run from unrelated cwd without --web-root. Missing packaged JS/CSS/index, checksum mismatch or wrong fixture health identity must fail instead of using source assets or another listener.

Exercise offline and live CLI against one singleton owner, actual MCP runtime idempotency/lease semantics, graceful shutdown with an active fixture, and process/port/lock cleanup. Include a controlled damaged-artifact negative scenario.

Test timeouts, interrupted requests, nonzero commands, native dependency failure, survivor children and redaction. Raw token/access records, database state and protocol traffic must not enter CI artifacts.

Run the documented local finite smoke and both real GitHub workflow jobs on the implementation PR, with sequential heavy verification and existing host/managed-project rules. Plan-only formatting validation does not claim a package or CI pass.
value: The owner avoids repeating installation checks, and other developers can try the experiment without reproducing the owner's machine.
